newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's ATX ends down, but boosted well off lows.
newsitem.headline: Austria's ATX ends down, but boosted well off lows.

text.p: Austria's blue-chip ATX index tumbled below the critical 1,400 point level on Wednesday in volatile trade but managed to heave itself above that level by the close.

The ATX, which ended 22.16 points or 1.55 percent lower at 1,408.14, bounced back from a session low of 1,379.71 as concerns of mounting inflation in the U.S. were allayed by softer-than-expected July retail sales data, traders said.
Trading was nervous ahead of tomorrow's expiry of August futures and options, and is expected to remain volatile into the expiry, they added.
"It would be better not to have any open positions tomorrow," said one.
"It's going to be interesting tomorrow. At 1215 it's expiry, at 1430 the U.S. jobs data come, and at 1500 we close -- and then we can see where we stand on Monday," he added.
The market will be closed on Friday for a public holiday.
The August ATX future ended 16.4 points down at 1,404.1 with 3,033 contracts traded. The contract is expected to settle at around 1,410 to 1,420 ATX points, a trader said.
Declining ATX issues overwhelmed gainers with 18 lower, two higher and one unchanged.
Leykam led decliners, falling 3.96 percent to 315 schillings, while Verbund was the top ATX gainer, adding on 0.29 percent to 877 schillings.
The broad-based Vienna bourse index ended 6.35 points or 1.24 percent lower at 507.36.
